newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CSN seen unhurt by chief's exit.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CSN seen unhurt by chief's exit.

text.p: The resignation of Companhia Siderurgica Nacional's (CSN) chief Sylvio Coutinho is unlikely to affect the firm or its share price but is an unwelcome sign of discord at the Brazilian steelmaker, analysts said.
"It won't affect the market price because CSN already trades at a discount, but it is not good," said one analyst, who asked not to be named.
A CSN spokesman said Coutinho tendered his resignation at a day-long board of directors at a meeting Tuesday in Sao Paulo.
He was company president until his official title was changed to director-superintendent for steel after a restructuring in May,

Market sources said Coutinho disagreed with plans to lay off some 2,000 workers. But the company spokesman denied there was any layoff program and said Coutinho's resignation was not related to the company's ongoing restructuring. But he declined to say why he quit.
The firm has about 13,700 employees, down nine percent from its workforce at the time of its privatization.

Analysts said it is too early to draw conclusions and it was unclear precisely why Coutinho stepped down. But they added the move was unlikely to affect either the company or CSN's share price significantly.
"There is no reason Coutinho's exit should affect the company's shares," said Pedro Martins, an analyst at Banco Patrimonio/Salomon Brothers.

One analyst described Coutinho, a long-time CSN employee popular with workers, as an expert in steel production who may be seen as out of step with the firm's ongoing diversification into energy and other fields as well as its restructuring.
"In this sense, his exit may signify an upside," he added.
Another analyst said Coutinho's exit will not be felt much because he had already lost power after the May restructuring, when economist Maria Silvia Bastos Marques was named chief financial officer.
Nonetheless, some analysts pointed to the development as a disturbing sign of continuing discord between the company's principal shareholders.
